about: The forge runtime's casting: what its worlds, tables and HUD ask for by role (roles), the ruin arena layouts, the conventions its pieces follow, the play data its generators read per piece (sections: sizes of slots, sockets, colliders, tiles, holds; no licence, hash or file here), and the name each piece has in its code (names: <forge name> -> <pack>/<asset> in the asset library, library/packs). The art itself, its licences and its bytes are the library's (builder/art/views.mjs); runtimes/forge/tools/library.mjs puts the two together into the catalog the kit's code reads.

conventions.characters: gf-humanoid-1 (research/gf-three/kit/character/RIG.md): faces +Z, sockets head, hand_r, hand_l, back; clips from clips/forge-humanoid-1.glb
conventions.weapons: origin = the grip (socket_grip), +Z = where it points, +Y = up, real size; socket_muzzle (guns, wand: where shots leave, +Z out), socket_grip_l (second hand), socket_tip (melee); `grip` = its place on a body's hand_r socket for third person, with a scale for the stylised bodies; `hold` = where fp/arms.glb's arm_r sits for it in first person
conventions.fp: fp/arms.glb is in camera space: the eye at the origin, looking down −Z (glTF camera), +Y up; socket_grip (right hand) takes a weapon's socket_grip, socket_grip_l the left hand
conventions.props: base at y = 0 and centred, unless origin is "grid" (KayKit Dungeon modular pieces on a 3 m grid); socket_flame on lit props (fire light and particles); parts are nodes that move (gate doors)
conventions.glow: enemy eyes are their own material `glow_eyes` (emissive, KHR_materials_emissive_strength): set its colour and strength per state (rest, tell +14% over the windup, white on hurt, 0 on death)
conventions.tint: player bodies: the hunters (track C3) carry `player_tint` (the dyed cloth: a greyscale copy of the texture, so the player colour multiplies the painted shading; listed in gf_body extras gfTint, gfTintMix 0.9); the KayKit spares `tint_cloth` (player-hooded) or `tint_cape` (player-knight, gfTintMix 0.85)
conventions.emissive: glowing parts are their own materials: glow_eyes (enemy eyes), glow_tip (a staff's or the focus's crystal), glow_coals (braziers), glow_flame (a lantern's panes); the Meshy ones keep the base texture as their emissive map, KHR_materials_emissive_strength
conventions.flash: guns (track C3) carry a muzzle flash: node `flash_muzzle` at socket_muzzle, material flash_muzzle (emissive (1.0, 0.48, 0.13), strength 4, double-sided), extras gfHidden: hidden by default, shown for 2–4 frames a shot
conventions.seats: `player.coop.seats` lists one body role per seat; seat n of 2–4 friends wears seats[n] in its own player colour
conventions.small: `small` maps a file to its small variant (small/…: the same model byte for byte with a 128–512 px picture; tools/small.mjs): what a game ships (kit/world.js and kit/wear.js `shipped`), for phones and for the texel look
conventions.world: world/ (tools/world.mjs): the arena's own code-made pieces and texel pictures at about 32 texels a metre; a piece's textureFiles name the pictures a texture slot can repaint

awaken.source: KayKit Skeletons_Awaken_Floor (Skeleton_Minion.glb): from lying in a heap to standing

taunt.source: KayKit Taunt (Skeleton_Minion.glb): a boss roar and stamp

windup.source: KayKit 1H_Melee_Attack_Chop 0–0.45 s over 0.3 s (the raise before the strike); play with hold, eye glow ramps alongside

lunge.source: KayKit 1H_Melee_Attack_Chop 0.45–0.66 s over 0.12 s (the strike, in place: the AI moves the body 0.5 m)

recover.source: KayKit 1H_Melee_Attack_Chop 0.66–1.07 s over 0.27 s (back to guard)

attack_unarmed.source: KayKit Unarmed_Melee_Attack_Punch_A (Knight.glb): a clawing lunge for an unarmed skeleton

cast_windup.source: KayKit Spellcast_Raise 0–0.5 s over 0.34 s (the ranged tell before cast)

hit_heavy.source: KayKit Hit_B (Knight.glb): a big hit that buckles the knees

hit_back.source: authored: KayKit Hit_A with its spine, head and hips motion turned 180° about Y (pushed forward); limbs at half

hit_left.source: authored: KayKit Hit_A turned 90° about Y (struck on its left side, it reels to its right); limbs at half

hit_right.source: authored: KayKit Hit_A turned −90° about Y (struck on its right side); limbs at half

block_hit.source: KayKit Block_Hit (Knight.glb): a shield takes a hit

shoot_2h.source: KayKit 2H_Ranged_Shoot (Knight.glb): a long gun at the shoulder

hold.note: the first-person hold: where the weapon's grip sits in camera space. arm_r (wave 3): with its family's hands (fp/hands-<family>.glb), the grip and the fist on it in view; bare (wave 2): the weapon alone on fp/rig.glb, the grip under the screen's edge. The rig's socket_grip turns and scales the weapon

fp/arms.glb.frame: camera space: the eye at the origin, looking down −Z, +Y up, metres; arm_r and arm_l are nodes the game moves

fp/gauntlet.glb.frame: the hand frame: origin where a handle passes through the fist, +X the way the knuckles point (the forearm runs back along −X), +Y the back of the hand, +Z the thumb's side; as drawn this is a left hand, a right hand is its mirror

cards/barrels.png.for: more pellets, or a wider spread

cards/repeater.png.for: a card that gives a repeater (a weapon that fires while held)

cards/saint.png.for: more damage paid for with health (a trade)

cards/scattergun.png.for: a card that gives a scattergun (a shotgun)

cards/scythe.png.for: a stronger or longer quick melee

cards/wind.png.for: more stamina, or stamina that comes back faster
